title: Results file
description:
One file per character per sim run, written by the gear sim and read by the armory planner. Keys are snake_case, and every object is strict.
The page also checks these rules, which this JSON Schema can't express, so a file that passes it can still be refused:
- default_fight_id names a fight in fights.
- Every fight_id in results, bag_upgrades results, bag_upgrades_all results, stat_weights and talents.best names a fight in fights.
- A bag upgrade's results have at most one entry per fight.
- bag_upgrades_all.results has exactly one result for each fight in fights.
- bag_upgrades_all needs two or more bag_upgrades, each in a different slot.
- sheet.weapon_skill.current is at most its max.
- Every gear in results is worn or a plan_id in plans.
- Every item_id in a plan's gear is that slot's worn item or one of its alternatives.
- slots has each slot exactly once.
- Every fight has a result for worn gear.
- Each fight_id in fights is unique.
- Each plan_id is unique.
- No item_id appears twice in one slot's alternatives.
- stat_weights has at most one entry per fight.
- Each Pawn label is unique.
- Each item_id in left_out_items is unique.
- No two results share a gear and fight.
- talents.best.ranks lists every talent in talents.yours exactly once, by talent_id.
- A talent's rank is at most its max_rank.
- No two talents in talents.yours share a tier and column.
- A chain fight has a setup.
- timeline is null on a chain fight's results (bag upgrade and bag_upgrades_all results too).
- pulls is null on a single fight's results (bag upgrade and bag_upgrades_all results too).
The runner must also keep these, which nothing checks:
- Each slot's alternatives come best first; the slot's badge shows the gain of the plan's item for that slot.
- talents.yours lists every talent in the tree, at rank 0 or more.
- character.professions names each profession as the game does (Leatherworking): the page matches them by name.
- Each quick_fixes text names the slot it is about; its slot is any slot or null, with no rule tying it to kind.

made_at.description: When the runner wrote this file.

export_saved_at.description: When the export this file came from was saved.

sample.description: true: a hand-made file; some numbers in it are made up.

provisional.description: true: the sim isn't matched to real fights yet.

left_out_items.description: Items the sim left out of every plan (a suspect item: no source and required level 1 or less, unless worn or in the bags). Recorded here, not in checks: checks are the accuracy gates the page counts. The page lists them under "Left out of the plan:" in How sure is this?, one line each: "Made-up Helm (12345), because it has no source and needs level 1." Absent: none recorded.

name.description: The left-out item's name, as the game has it.

reason.description: The left-out item's reason, said after "because": "it has no source and needs level 1". The page adds the full stop.

name.description: For display only: never a key, and never in a file name or path.

character_key.description: A random id the export addon mints once per character (export format 7). It joins this file with the engagement-score file.

professions.description: The character's professions at export, e.g. Leatherworking 165 of 225. The page matches them by name only, to tell items you can craft yourself; skill and max are carried, unused for now. Absent or an empty list: none.

sheet_buffed.description: true: the game's sheet as it showed at export, with the buffs that were up.

weapon_skill.description: The weapon skill for the main-hand weapon at export, e.g. Two-Handed Axes 148 of 150. The sheet shows it as "Axe skill 148/150". Absent or null: not exported (the sheet leaves that line out).

weapon_type.description: The main-hand weapon's skill, by the game's name for it: "Two-Handed Axes", "Staves", "One-Handed Maces", "Fist Weapons". The sheet says it short: "Two-Handed Axes" reads "Axe skill"; a name the page doesn't know is shown as given.

fight_id.description: A sim fight type. A real logged fight is an engagement_id, which only the engagement-score file has.

duration_s.description: The fight length in seconds. On a chain fight, the length of one pull.

melee_miss_pct.description: The chance, in percent, that a melee swing misses this fight's target, with the sheet's melee_hit_pct. The page says it under the enemy level: With 0 hit, you miss 8.0% of melee swings at level 33. Absent or null: not simmed (the sentence is left out).

setup.description: Required on a chain fight; may be absent on a single fight.

default_fight_id.description: The fight the page opens on: one of fights.

data.description: classic: the item's stats and source may predate Forever.

worn.description: Null: nothing equipped in this slot.

imbue.description: The temporary weapon imbue on the worn item at export (Windfury Weapon, a poison, a sharpening stone), for the weapon slots. The page names the main hand's in the header: "Guardian's Dualblade with Windfury Weapon." Absent or null: none, or not exported (the header names the weapon alone).

data.description: classic: the item's stats and source may predate Forever.

gain_ep.description: EP gained over what is worn.

gain_dps.description: DPS gained over what is worn, for weapons. The page shows gain_ep when it is not null, and this only in its absence.

alternatives.description: Best first, which this schema doesn't check. The slot's badge shows the gain of the alternative the plan puts in the slot.

slots.description: One entry per slot, each slot exactly once.

data.description: classic: the item's stats and source may predate Forever.

results.description: What you wear with this bag item put on in its slot, everything else worn: one result per fight, shaped like results (no gear). The page's Equip button swaps the slot and shows these in place of worn's results; Undo swaps back. Absent or null: not simmed (no Equip button).

out_of_mana_s.description: Seconds to the first out of mana (the sim's tto); on a chain fight, wall time from the start of the first pull, gaps included. On a chain fight the page says the pull this falls in ran dry: pull k runs from (k-1)*(duration_s + gap_s) to that plus duration_s (setup.gap_s); a time in the gap after a pull counts as the next pull (you start it with no mana), and a time past the last pull is said as a time. "never": simmed, and it never runs dry in this fight. Null: not simmed.

time_to_die_s.description: Seconds to die. Null: not simmed.

timeline.description: DPS and mana over the fight. Single fights only: null on a chain fight. Null on a single fight: no timeline in this file.

mana_end.description: The mana left at the end of the pull. A pull that ran dry can end a little above 0 (the sim regains some after running out), so the page doesn't read it to say which pull ran dry: out_of_mana_s says that.

pulls.description: DPS and mana per pull. Chain fights only: null on a single fight. The pull that ran dry is the one out_of_mana_s falls in, not one whose mana_end is 0. Null on a chain fight: no pull data in this file.

school.description: The spell school of this part of the damage: physical for melee swings and weapon procs. The page colours the split by it. Absent or null: not simmed (the page colours parts by order and leaves out "Colour is the spell school.").

bag_upgrades_all.description: What you wear with every bag upgrade put on together, everything else worn: one result per fight, shaped like results (no gear). Only with two or more bag_upgrades, each in a different slot. The page's Equip all button shows these in place of worn's results; Undo takes them all off. Absent or null: not simmed (no Equip all button).

out_of_mana_s.description: Seconds to the first out of mana (the sim's tto); on a chain fight, wall time from the start of the first pull, gaps included. On a chain fight the page says the pull this falls in ran dry: pull k runs from (k-1)*(duration_s + gap_s) to that plus duration_s (setup.gap_s); a time in the gap after a pull counts as the next pull (you start it with no mana), and a time past the last pull is said as a time. "never": simmed, and it never runs dry in this fight. Null: not simmed.

time_to_die_s.description: Seconds to die. Null: not simmed.

timeline.description: DPS and mana over the fight. Single fights only: null on a chain fight. Null on a single fight: no timeline in this file.

mana_end.description: The mana left at the end of the pull. A pull that ran dry can end a little above 0 (the sim regains some after running out), so the page doesn't read it to say which pull ran dry: out_of_mana_s says that.

pulls.description: DPS and mana per pull. Chain fights only: null on a single fight. The pull that ran dry is the one out_of_mana_s falls in, not one whose mana_end is 0. Null on a chain fight: no pull data in this file.

school.description: The spell school of this part of the damage: physical for melee swings and weapon procs. The page colours the split by it. Absent or null: not simmed (the page colours parts by order and leaves out "Colour is the spell school.").

quick_fixes.description: Fixes that need no new gear, and what each is worth: imbue (a missing weapon imbue), empty_slot (a slot with nothing in it) or weapon_skill (weapon skill under its cap). slot is the slot it concerns, or null; no rule ties it to kind. dps_gain is the DPS the fix is worth; text says the fix and names the slot. Absent or an empty list: none.

gear.description: An item_id for each of the 17 slots: the slot's worn item or one of its alternatives. Null: the plan puts nothing in that slot.

reach.description: How far each role's slider can go, 0 to 100, while this plan is the one the sliders pick: the items the sim knows can't reach further with this plan's mix. 100: no limit. The page draws the part past it hatched, says Can reach N with this mix (No limit with this mix at 100), and stops a slider there. Absent or null: not simmed (no reach is shown and the sliders aren't stopped).

gear.description: worn, or a plan_id in plans.

out_of_mana_s.description: Seconds to the first out of mana (the sim's tto); on a chain fight, wall time from the start of the first pull, gaps included. On a chain fight the page says the pull this falls in ran dry: pull k runs from (k-1)*(duration_s + gap_s) to that plus duration_s (setup.gap_s); a time in the gap after a pull counts as the next pull (you start it with no mana), and a time past the last pull is said as a time. "never": simmed, and it never runs dry in this fight. Null: not simmed.

time_to_die_s.description: Seconds to die. Null: not simmed.

timeline.description: DPS and mana over the fight. Single fights only: null on a chain fight. Null on a single fight: no timeline in this file.

mana_end.description: The mana left at the end of the pull. A pull that ran dry can end a little above 0 (the sim regains some after running out), so the page doesn't read it to say which pull ran dry: out_of_mana_s says that.

pulls.description: DPS and mana per pull. Chain fights only: null on a single fight. The pull that ran dry is the one out_of_mana_s falls in, not one whose mana_end is 0. Null on a chain fight: no pull data in this file.

school.description: The spell school of this part of the damage: physical for melee swings and weapon procs. The page colours the split by it. Absent or null: not simmed (the page colours parts by order and leaves out "Colour is the spell school.").

source.description: Where these weights came from. precomputed: simmed ahead of time for the character's class, spec and level band (level_min to level_max), not this gear; the page says so. yours: simmed for this character's gear. Absent: simmed for the character, and the page says nothing about it.

points.description: The talent points spent in this tree: the sum of the ranks in yours, which this schema doesn't check. The page shows it on the talents pill: "22 pts".

yours.description: Every talent in the tree, at rank 0 or more, which this schema doesn't check.

best.description: The best build the sim found: a rank for every talent in yours, and its DPS gain in the fight fight_id. Null: no best build in this file.
